title: NETBCI2026: NETBCI: longitudinal right-hand motor imagery vs rest BCI training
description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of 19 healthy right-handed participants trained over four sessions on separate days to control a brain-computer interface. Participants used sustained right-hand grasping motor imagery versus rest to move a cursor on a one-dimensional two-target task with online visual feedback. Each session comprised six feedback runs, giving 14,431 trials in total. The recordings were made with a 74-channel EEG system alongside MEG and are organized in BIDS format.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 250 Hz from 74 passive Ag/AgCl Easycap electrodes, referenced to the mastoids, simultaneously with a MEGIN TRIUX MEG system, and BCI2000 was used for acquisition and feedback. Each trial had a 1 s inter-stimulus interval followed by a 5 s target presentation, with cursor feedback from 3 to 6 s. Participants performed right-hand motor imagery for the up target and rested for the down target, with 6 runs of up to 32 trials per session.
